simple.meaning: הוּם (hûwm) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to make an uproar , or agitate greatly.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 5 times across Ruth, 1 Samuel, 1 Kings, Psalms, Micah, beginning at Ruth 1:19. Its contexts include covenant, kingship, priesthood, prophetic witness, city, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הוּם (H1949).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: הוּם (hûwm) / H1949 is traced through Ruth 1:19, 1 Samuel 4:5, 1 Kings 1:45, Psalms 55:3 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: So they both went until they came to Bethlehem. When they had come to Bethlehem, all the city was excited about them, and they asked, “Is this Naomi?”
When the ark of Yahweh’s covenant came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth resounded.
